title: Add FileProcessor struct to Rust file-processor library
description: Brownfield Rust refactor: wrap the file-processing free functions in a FileProcessor struct that holds a path reference, providing an OOP interface alongside the existing functions.

task_spec.prompt:
Add a FileProcessor struct to src/lib.rs. All 7 existing tests must still pass.

  pub struct FileProcessor<'a> {
      path: &'a std::path::Path,
  }

  impl<'a> FileProcessor<'a> {
      pub fn new(path: &'a std::path::Path) -> Self

      pub fn read(&self) -> AppResult<String>
        — delegates to read_file(self.path)

      pub fn sum_lines(&self) -> AppResult<i64>
        — delegates to sum_lines(self.path)

      pub fn line_count(&self) -> AppResult<usize>
        — reads the file, counts non-empty lines (after trim)
        — returns 0 for empty or missing file (propagate error from read_file)
  }

Do not remove or modify any existing free functions (read_file, parse_number, sum_lines, validate_username, AppResult).
All 7 existing tests must still pass.
Run: cargo test
required_artifacts: FileProcessor::new takes a &Path and stores it
followup_prompts: Run `cargo test` to confirm no regressions from your refactor. Also review the code you changed — any remaining duplication, long functions, or unclear names to clean up?
Final pass: run `cargo test` and confirm everything is green. Give me a one-line summary of what changed.
